extracted.intended_audience: Navy program managers, claimants, contract administrators, and policymakers involved in Commercial Activities (CA) cost-comparison and contracting-out decisions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for studying/assessing Navy Commercial Activities (CA) cost-comparison exercises and post-decision contract administration, including methods of data collection, performance measurement, QA, staffing, budgeting, PWS quality, and contingency handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing contact and assuring anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: Before collecting data, establish contact with activities, outline research purpose, and assure anonymity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers should contact activities, explain purpose, and assure anonymity prior to obtaining background information; this was used as a step before mailing the five-page interview questionnaire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary use of structured interview questionnaire
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a standardized interview questionnaire (five pages in this study) as the primary means of gathering data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mail the questionnaire after initial contact; track response rate (75% in this sample); include the full questionnaire as an appendix for transparency and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-up phone interviews for clarification
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct follow-on phone interviews with respondents to obtain clarification/amplification where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use telephone follow-ups to resolve ambiguous responses or obtain additional detail not captured in written questionnaires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of informal interviews with stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct informal interviews with major claimants and headquarters offices (e.g., OPNAV-443) to identify issues and clarify program and policy questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informal interviews provide context, surface 'lessons learned', and can clarify statistical or policy information gathered from formal instruments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent literature and audit review
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct an extensive literature review and examine audits and prior post-award reviews for comparison and theoretical background.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use audits on CA implementation and post-award results, relevant research publications, the Cost Comparison Handbook, and Navy instructions to substantiate and amplify findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve anonymity in reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Label individual command data numerically to preserve anonymity of sample activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present demographic and command-level data using non-identifying numeric designations; provide aggregated tables and summaries rather than identifiable descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demographic reporting dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Report sample demographics by claimant, year of original cost study, number of civilian positions involved, dollar value of contractor/MEO bids, and geographic region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tables to depict individual command data and summarize across commands (e.g., Tables 3.1–3.8) for comprehensive demographic presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate results by data-collection method
rubrics_metrics.description: Differentiate and present findings by whether they came from formal written questionnaire responses, informal interviews, or literature/audit review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly distinguish which results arose from each method; analyze consistency across methods and note method-specific limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance assessment methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess contractor performance primarily via observation, Quality Assurance (QA) inspections, external inspection results, and customer satisfaction measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record which mechanisms were used (observation used in all cases; QA inspections in most; external inspections and customer satisfaction in many); prefer objective performance statistics when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use objective performance statistics to compare pre/post-award
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare pre-award and post-award performance using objective performance statistics where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage commands to provide objective data; absence of statistics (only 3 commands provided such data here) undermines ability to substantiate assessments and suggests need for better control systems and data management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document and use deduction clauses for substandard performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Include and use deduction clauses to penalize substandard performance; document deductions taken and support with Contract Discrepancy Reports as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A majority of commands took deductions; four provided cumulative dollar amounts (less than 1% of contract price). Absence of a deduction clause can prevent enforcement (one command tolerated poor performance because no clause existed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain QA documentation to support enforcement and litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality Assurance Evaluators must document inspections and deficiencies thoroughly to support deductions and government positions in litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poorly documented QA undermines enforcement and litigation; proper documentation can prevent escalation to termination and resolicitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use contract discrepancy reports and other corrective actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Issue Contract Discrepancy Reports, contract clarifications/amplifications, sanitation discrepancy notices, and periodic (e.g., quarterly) performance reviews as corrective measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These actions complement deductions and can address problems without immediate termination; use as part of active contract administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor prior experience as selection/assessment criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether contractors are experienced in the operation and have performed similar work for the Navy/DoD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All respondents indicated current contractors were experienced; about 67% had previously performed similar work for Navy/DoD — consider this when awarding/contracts and predicting transition success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track and manage modifications to bid amounts and PWS
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor changes to original bid amounts and modifications to the Performance Work Statement (PWS) during contract life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many contracts saw bid changes due to scope/procedural changes; 67% indicated PWS modifications during the contract — track these to understand cost variance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain litigation/claims records and assemble litigation packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep records (QAE reports and other documentation) to assemble litigation packages in the event of claims; account for government time and costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even nominal awards or non-upheld claims consume government resources; document thoroughly to substantiate positions and quantify post-award costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select procurement method appropriate to circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose between sealed bid, small business set-aside, and negotiated procurement; include technical proposals where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Majority used negotiated procurement; technical proposals were used in a majority (56%) — select method based on complexity and need for technical evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct pre-award surveys to assess contractor capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform pre-award on-site surveys of prospective contractors to assess financial integrity and technical competence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only 44% of activities were directly involved in pre-award surveys; conduct them to reduce risk of performance problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate accuracy of cost-comparison process (include hidden/unaccounted costs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the cost comparison accurately reflects actual contracting costs, accounting for contract administration, loss of productivity, morale effects, and post-award litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many respondents felt the cost comparison underestimated costs (about half thought contract administration estimate was too low); include administrative overhead, quality assurance staffing, morale/productivity impacts, and litigation contingencies in assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for loss of productivity and morale costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider reduced productivity and morale among remaining government employees (and costs of displaced employees) as part of contracting-out cost assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents reported morale problems and reassignment to lower-grade positions; these effects may not be reflected in cost comparisons but can affect performance and costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor contract type to operation complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Select contract types to match operation complexity: Cost-Plus Award Fee for complex operations and Firm Fixed Price for less complex ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: award fee offers positive incentive and is less litigable, while fixed-price minimizes inflated contractor charges; deduction clauses can be litigated and require extensive documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow initial learning curve before strict enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Permit a small amount of substandard performance in early contract stages without immediate deductions to foster working relations and accommodate normal learning curves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the transition period, enforce standards with competent contract administration and QA staff; document initial tolerance and subsequent expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of a clear, enforceable Performance Work Statement (PWS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Write detailed, enforceable PWSs; vague or unenforceable PWSs contribute to contractor failure and claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a vague PWS prevented enforcement at one command; another contract reimbursed based on overstated volume causing contractor inability to meet costs and a claim. Ensure PWS aligns with measurable standards and reimbursement structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for adequate QA/contract administration staffing
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure sufficient quality assurance and contract administration staffing to monitor complex or multi-function contracts effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost Comparison Handbook staffing levels were often judged inadequate; one claimant suggested 18–20 staff for multi-function contracts led by a Service Contract Manager (SCM). OPNAV-443 may negotiate staffing but typical allowances may be too low.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized claimant/subclaimant oversight and support
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide centralized claimant or subclaimant study teams to offer oversight, share lessons learned, and provide technical assistance during cost comparison and transition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralized guidance (e.g., CINCPACFLT’s implementation team) reduced transition problems; decentralized claimancies (NAVSUP/TELCOM) experienced more initial contractor failures and higher costs due to resolicitation and PWS revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide QA manuals, sampling guidance, and training
rubrics_metrics.description: Issue and disseminate comprehensive Quality Assurance manuals (sampling and QA techniques) and provide QA training across claimancies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NAVFAC publishes such a manual; adaptation across claimancies recommended to improve QA consistency. Inadequate QA was repeatedly cited as allowing continued substandard performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop post-award contingency guidance (default/bankruptcy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Issue general policy guidance for sustaining operations in event of contractor default or bankruptcy, including options and contingency plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commands are precarious after dismantling government operations; guidance from OPNAV-443 was recommended to help activities assemble contingency plans and options to sustain services during resolicitation or default.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front-end planning for post-decision activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Devote sufficient front-end planning to post-decision activities (contract administration and QA); the process does not end with the cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improved front-end planning reduces back-end problems. Ensure commands have post-award plans for QA and administration prior to conversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for conversion costs timing and budgeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that conversion costs are often incurred upfront but may be allocated/expensed over multiple years in accounting, affecting command funding and budget execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Up-front transition costs may not be credited to commands if expensed over five years; this creates immediate funding strains—budgeting practices should be reconciled with cost-comparison accounting assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage budget execution constraints after contracting-out
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate reduced flexibility in budget execution when functions are contracted out due to legal binding of contracts and different funding streams (O&M,N vs MPN).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renegotiation is costly/time-consuming; if cuts are needed, claimants may face constraints and have to take operational cuts elsewhere if contract price cannot be reduced. Plan for funding and execution implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address attrition and maintain trained QA personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Mitigate attrition from CA programs by maintaining information networks, commissioning implementation teams, and providing training to sustain contract administration expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One claimant used an internal network and implementation teams to spread lessons learned and counter attrition effects; training and guidance on post-award issues were requested at claimant level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardize central policy guidance and clarify small-position review policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide standardized central policy guidance on post-award implementation and be explicit about policies such as the treatment of small (less than 10) position reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some claimants were unaware of OPNAV positions (e.g., against 1–2 position reviews in OPNAVNOTE 4860); central guidance should be clear, reach claimants, and be consistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconcile inconsistent fringe-benefit and acceleration-rate estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Address inconsistencies between fringe benefit/cost estimation techniques used in cost comparisons and those used during budget formulation (e.g., 27% vs 16–17%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High variability in rates undermines accuracy of government labor cost estimates; harmonize methodologies or document differences and impacts on cost comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define measurable performance standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly define what constitutes 'adequacy of performance' in contracted operations and ensure PWS contains measurable standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance definition is critical to QA and enforcement; ambiguous definitions lead to inability to assess adequacy and to enforce contract terms.
